## Question 1 (4 points)

Let $X_i \sim N(20, 2)$ for $i = 1,2, \dots, 50$ and assume these are independent. What are the following?

-   $\text{E}[20\bar{X} + 4]$
-   $\text{SD}[30\bar{X} - 5]$

[We have the following:]{style="color: red;"}

-   [$\text{E}[20\bar{X} + 4] = 404$]{style="color: red;"}
-   [$\text{SD}[30\bar{X} - 5] = \sqrt{900 \times \frac{4}{50}} = 30 \times \frac{2}{\sqrt{50}} \simeq 8.4853$]{style="color: red;"}

## Question 2A (9 points)

Let $X_i \sim N(10, 3)$ and $Y_i \sim N(20, 4)$ for $i = 1, 2, 3, \dots, 30$ and assume independence between all $X_i$ and $Y_i$. What is the sampling distribution of $\bar{X} + \bar{Y}$? Replace the $a$, $b$ and $c$ in the formula below with the correct values.

$$
\bar{X} + \bar{Y} \sim N\left(30, \frac{5}{\sqrt{30}} \right)
$$

Hint: Find the sampling distributions of $\bar{X}$ and $\bar{Y}$ first and then use the theorems regarding the expectation and variance of a linear combination of two independent random variables. Also, be sure to be careful when distinguishing between variance and standard deviation when applying these theorems.

[We have that $\bar{X} \sim N\left(10, \frac{3}{\sqrt{30}} \right)$ and $\bar{Y} \sim N\left(20, \frac{4}{\sqrt{30}} \right)$.]{style="color: red;"}

[We know that $\text{E}[X + Y] = \text{E}[X] + \text{E}[Y]$ so then $\text{E}[\bar{X} + \bar{Y}] = 10 + 20 = 30$. We know also know that for independent $X$ and $Y$ that $\text{Var}[X + Y] = \text{Var}[X] + \text{Var}[Y]$ so then $\text{Var}[\bar{X} + \bar{Y}] = \text{Var}[\bar{X}] + \text{Var}[\bar{Y}] = \frac{9}{30} + \frac{16}{30} = \frac{25}{30}$. This means that $\text{SD}[\bar{X} + \bar{Y}] = \sqrt{\text{Var}[\bar{X} + \bar{Y}]} = \frac{5}{\sqrt{30}}$. Thus,]{style="color: red;"}

$$
\bar{X} + \bar{Y} \sim N\left(30, \frac{5}{\sqrt{30}} \right)
$$

## Question 2B (5 points)

Complete the code block below to simulate draws from the sampling distribution of $\bar{X} + \bar{Y}$ from the previous question. Then compute the mean and standard deviation of the simulated draws and create a histogram of the draws.

```{r, echo = TRUE}
set.seed(100)

n_draws <- 100000 # Number of draws/simulations
n <- 30 # Sample size
xybars <- rep(0, n_draws) # Vector to stores draws for sum of sample means

mu_X <- 10
mu_Y <- 20
sigma_X <- 3
sigma_Y <- 4

for (i in 1:n_draws){
  x_sample <- rnorm(n, mu_X, sigma_X)
  y_sample <- rnorm(n, mu_Y, sigma_Y)
  
  xbar <- mean(x_sample)
  ybar <- mean(y_sample)
  xybars[i] <- xbar + ybar
}

mean(xybars)
sd(xybars)

hist(xybars)
```

## Question 3 (5 points)

Let $X_i \sim N(180, 10)$ for $i = 1, 2, 3, \dots, 64$. In the code block below, compute the following probabilities:

-   $P(\bar{X} < 179)$
-   $P(\bar{X} > 182)$
-   $P(179 < \bar{X} < 182)$

```{r, echo = TRUE}
mu23 <- 180
sigma23 <- 10
n23 <- 64

# You could do it this way

pnorm(179, mu23, sigma23/sqrt(n23))
1-pnorm(182, mu23, sigma23/sqrt(n23))
pnorm(182, mu23, sigma23/sqrt(n23)) - pnorm(179, mu23, sigma23/sqrt(n23))

# Or you could do it this way

pnorm((179-mu23)/(sigma23/sqrt(n23)))
1-pnorm((182-mu23)/(sigma23/sqrt(n23)))
pnorm((182-mu23)/(sigma23/sqrt(n23))) - pnorm((179-mu23)/(sigma23/sqrt(n23)))
```

## Question 4 (6 points)

Let $X_i \sim N(10, 2)$ for $i = 1,2,3,\dots, 50$. In the code block below, compute the following percentiles for $\bar{X}$:

-   $85^{th}$ percentile
-   $20^{th}$ percentile
-   $1^{st}$ and $3^{rd}$ quartiles
-   The median

```{r, echo = TRUE}
mu24 <- 10
sigma24 <- 2
n24 <- 50

# You could do it this way

qnorm(0.85, mu24, sigma24/sqrt(n24))
qnorm(0.2, mu24, sigma24/sqrt(n24))
qnorm(0.25, mu24, sigma24/sqrt(n24))
qnorm(0.75, mu24, sigma24/sqrt(n24))
qnorm(0.5, mu24, sigma24/sqrt(n24))

# Or you could do it this way

qnorm(0.85)*sigma24/sqrt(n24) + mu24
qnorm(0.2)*sigma24/sqrt(n24) + mu24
qnorm(0.25)*sigma24/sqrt(n24) + mu24
qnorm(0.75)*sigma24/sqrt(n24) + mu24
qnorm(0.5)*sigma24/sqrt(n24) + mu24
```
